newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn basis firms after sharp drop.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - Corn basis firms after sharp drop.

text.p: FOB Gulf basis values for corn recovered slightly on Wednesday after crashing 44 cents per bushel on Tuesday as light buying interest re-emerged into the market, several grain dealers said.
"It's starting to come back a little," one dealer said. "We're seeing a little more buying interest."
Bids firmed five cents for September 11-30 delivery, but dealers were wary of predicting prices had bottomed out. "It's a bit too early to get that optimistic," one dealer said.
Bids had fallen sharply during the week as newly harvested corn from the U.S. south and southeast flooded the market.
Also, export demand was said to be slack.
Soybean bids fell slightly in quiet dealings.
Wheat bids were mostly steady.
Dealers quoted the following afternoon FOB U.S. Gulf values, basis Chicago futures, except hard red winter wheat basis Kansas City. (In cents per bushel).
